A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CurES research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures and case studies, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments, learning curves, sampling analyses and case studies for CurES and its baselines.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds component ablations, baseline comparisons, additional model evaluations and elapsed-time measurements.

M1.justification: Prompt sampling, variance-based rollout allocation and Bayesian updating remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 clarifies stages and budget notation. The loss-normalization correction matches the estimator already used in v1's appendix derivation and does not establish a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Numina-Math and the same eight evaluation benchmarks: MATH500, GSM8K, GAO23, MINERVA, OlympiadBench, AIME24, AIME25 and AMC23. The additional model families do not introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds actual DAPO and MoPPS comparisons against CurES-GRPO in Table 3, substantially extending the evaluated comparator set. Figure 11 also includes Speed-RL and GVM alongside GRPO in the new elapsed-time comparison. Table 1's original comparators remain.

E3.justification: V2 extends evaluation to Llama3.2-3B-Instruct and Phi-4-mini-Instruct, introduces elapsed training time as an efficiency measure, and adds component-removal controls. The original Qwen training settings and Pass@1/Average@16 evaluation remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: New Table 2 independently removes rollout allocation and prompt sampling, directly testing the contributions of the two central components. V1 contained sampling-budget sensitivity analyses but lacked these component ablations. Existing gradient analyses, sampling studies and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that AIME24, AIME25 and AMC23 results are averaged over 16 runs. V2 adds no new seed information, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 and Figures 1–10 retain their results. New Table 2 reports averages of 43.71 and 44.08 for the ablations versus 44.94 for full CurES; Table 3 adds DAPO at 42.80 and MoPPS at 43.98. Table 4 reports CurES/GRPO averages of 34.30/31.29 for Llama and 40.12/39.06 for Phi. Figure 11 newly reports approximately 4.51-fold and 3.86-fold elapsed-time speedups over GRPO.

T1.justification: V2 inserts the missing 1/m factor into the empirical-loss definitions in Equations 16 and 52. This restores consistency with the averaging already present in v1's Equations 53 and 56. The remaining assumptions, bounds and appendix derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract adds a claimed 2.12-point advantage over the best prior sample-efficient methods, extending the headline comparison beyond GRPO. The introduction foregrounds state-of-the-art performance and 5.5-fold acceleration, although that acceleration was already reported in v1's Section 5.3. The central theoretical and algorithmic contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly interprets the component ablations as demonstrating complementary contributions and the Llama/Phi results as supporting generalizability across architectures. It also interprets the timing results as practical acceleration. Existing mechanism explanations and the distribution-shift caveat remain, without substantive new limitations.

D1.justification: Figure 11 and Appendix B newly disclose absolute training times, including 4.5 versus 20.1 hours for the 1.5B comparison. The VERL setup, learning rate, rollout settings and code-access link remain unchanged. Hardware and detailed timing methodology are still unspecified.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands discussion of self-evolving curricula, rollout downsampling and Bayesian task sampling, adding works by Chen et al., Xu et al., Wang et al. and Qu et al. (2025b). This refines positioning while retaining the original rationale for jointly optimizing prompt sampling and rollout allocation.

P1.justification: V2 revises the related-work discussion, explains the algorithm's two stages more explicitly, and refines the sampling-budget discussion. Appendix B is retitled Extended Experimental Results, and the preprint header becomes an ICLR 2026 publication header. The overall narrative and section sequence remain stable.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation expands with three new tables and Figure 11's two elapsed-time panels with zoomed insets. Table 1 and Figure 3 are relocated, and several captions are revised. Existing figure graphics and case-study displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 2–4 and Figure 11 strengthen support for the existing claims by testing component contributions, elapsed-time efficiency and performance beyond Qwen and the original comparators. The normalization correction also improves mathematical consistency. These gains are limited by sparse details for the new experiments and unchanged uncertainty reporting. The new abstract additionally overstates the comparator margin: Table 3 reports 44.94 versus 43.98 for MoPPS, a 0.96-point advantage rather than 2.12.
